issues.passage: The reforms were designed to subvert authoritarian rule by expanding voting access and oversight.
issues.why: Undermining authoritarian power by expanding voting access and oversight is a valid, natural use of subvert = undermine the power or authority of. A student who knows the definition would accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: Satire can subvert official narratives by exposing their contradictions.
wrongPassages: Party loyalists moved to subvert the dictator by defending every decree and packing the courts with allies.
They hoped to subvert the constitution by enforcing its amendments more strictly.
She sought to subvert the chair's authority by carefully following every rule the chair had set.

issues.passage: Researchers called the data set scanty after every variable had been measured in triplicate.
issues.why: Measuring each variable in triplicate describes method, not quantity. A small sample measured three times is still scanty, so this remains correct use of scanty = small or insufficient in quantity.

fix.correctPassage: Evidence for the theory remains scanty and contested.
wrongPassages: The harvest was scanty: silos overflowed and crews still left grain in the fields.
Her scanty briefing covered risks, costs, and a recommendation across four full slides.
Researchers called the data set scanty after logging millions of observations across every relevant variable.
